'admx' means it was extracted from the policy definitions Microsoft ships on the target OS itself - the authoritative declaration for that build - not from a web page.
_dates: There is no file-level collection date. This ledger is appended to as facts are measured, and the single field that used to be here read 2026-08-27 while 22 rows carried dates from 2026-08-28 to 2026-09-02 - among them at13-fix-remeasured-retention-11s-to-24h, which it dated before the run that produced it. Every row dates itself in its own source, and that is the only date that can stay right.

facts.source: PowerShellExecutionPolicy.admx, policy EnableScriptBlockLogging, enabledValue decimal 1
facts.notes: class=Both, so a User-scope twin exists; this toolkit writes the Machine scope only. Sibling element EnableScriptBlockInvocationLogging (DWord) logs start/stop of every block - very high volume, left off by default. PROVEN: 4104 events appear for script blocks in a NEW powershell session after -Apply.

facts.notes: PROVEN on the lab: after -Apply, 4103 module-logging events appear in Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational. The '*' = '*' pair is what enables all modules.

facts.notes: Sibling elements: OutputDirectory (text/String), EnableInvocationHeader (boolean/DWord). PROVEN: transcripts were written into a yyyyMMdd subfolder of OutputDirectory (e.g. Transcripts\20260823\PowerShell_transcript.<host>.<id>.<stamp>.txt).

facts.notes: Note the key is under Software\Microsoft\..., NOT Software\Policies\Microsoft\... - unlike every other policy here. Puts the command line into event 4688. PROVEN: event 4688 carried 'Process Command Line: "C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe" /c ...' immediately after -Apply, with no reboot.

facts.source: EventLog.admx, Channel_LogMaxSize_* with minValue=20480 maxValue=2147483647; channels declared: Application, Security, Setup, System
facts.notes: PROVEN in kilobytes by measurement: a policy value of 1048576 produced a channel maxSize of 1073741824 bytes (exactly 1048576 * 1024), read via 'wevtutil gl Security'. REQUIRES A REBOOT: unchanged after 'gpupdate /target:computer /force', correct after restart.

facts.source: WindowsFirewall.admx, policies WF_Logging_Name_1 (DomainProfile) and WF_Logging_Name_2 (StandardProfile); LogFileSize minValue=128 maxValue=32767
facts.notes: IMPORTANT: only DomainProfile and StandardProfile declare a Logging policy. There is NO PublicProfile logging policy in the ADMX - a host on a public network is not covered by this setting. StandardProfile is what the modern UI calls the Private profile. PROVEN on the lab, with two caveats found by running it: (1) the firewall service runs as NT Authority\LocalService, so a directory granting only SYSTEM and Administrators leaves it unable to write and no log ever appears - NT SERVICE\mpssvc needs an explicit Modify grant, and that service SID does resolve via NTAccount.Translate; (2) logging starts only after a REBOOT.

facts.source: measured on the lab, Windows Server 2019 build 17763
facts.notes: TRAP. DISM and ServerManager report contradictory state for PowerShell 2.0 on the same host at the same moment: Get-WindowsOptionalFeature said MicrosoftWindowsPowerShellV2 = Enabled while Get-WindowsFeature said PowerShell-V2 = Removed. A script auditing with either one alone gives a wrong answer. IronBlackBox acts on the DISM view (it exists on client and server) and reports the disagreement rather than picking a winner silently.

facts.source: measured on the lab
facts.notes: PowerShell 2.0 requires the .NET 2.0 CLR, shipped with .NET Framework 3.5. With NDP\v3.5 absent and NetFx3 DisabledWithPayloadRemoved, 'powershell.exe -Version 2 -Command "exit 0"' exits -65536 and the engine cannot run AT ALL - even though DISM reports the feature Enabled. So feature state is not the same question as exposure, and the exposure question is answered by trying to launch it. Only the exit code is usable: the child's error text comes back as UTF-16 mojibake through a captured pipe.

facts.source: decoded the live descriptors on the lab and confirmed functionally
facts.notes: Event channel access masks: 0x1 read, 0x2 write, 0x4 CLEAR, 0xF0000 the standard rights. Server 2019 Security channel as shipped: SYSTEM 0xF0005, BUILTIN\Administrators 0x5 (read+CLEAR), Event Log Readers 0x1 - so an administrator can erase the Security log and needs no WRITE_DAC to do it. PROVEN functionally: after removing 0x4 from Administrators, 'wevtutil cl Application' returns exit 5 'Access is denied.', and after rollback it returns 0 again.

facts.source: measured on the lab
facts.notes: TRAP, and the one that produced a published defect in this project's predecessor. DiscretionaryAcl.RemoveAccess('Allow', sid, 0x4, 'None') left the Administrators mask at 0x7 UNCHANGED while happily regenerating a valid-looking descriptor - the API returned no error and removed nothing. Use SetAccess with an explicitly computed mask, then RE-READ the descriptor and assert the bit is gone. Never trust an ACL helper's return.

facts.source: measured on the lab
facts.notes: .NET regenerates a descriptor using rights abbreviations (CCDCLC) where Windows prints hex (0x7). Identical meaning, completely different text. Comparing descriptors as STRINGS therefore reports a change that did not happen and rewrites the channel on every run. All comparison must decode to per-SID masks.

facts.source: EventLog.admx enabledValue is <string>1</string>; written and read back on the lab
facts.notes: Retention and AutoBackupLogFiles are REG_SZ, not DWord. Semantics from Microsoft's own ADML help text: Retention enabled + log full = 'new events are not written to the log and are lost' - the log STOPS RECORDING. AutoBackupLogFiles only takes effect when Retention is enabled, and turns a full log into a renamed archive plus a fresh file. So Retention alone is the worst available setting, and Retention plus AutoBackup is the only combination that loses nothing. Write AutoBackup FIRST so the pair never passes through the dangerous state.

facts.source: measured on the lab
facts.notes: The MaxSize registry policy overrides the channel's local configuration: 'wevtutil sl <ch> /ms:1052672' did not stick while the policy specified 262144 KB. Consequence for testing: a log rollover cannot be forced by shrinking the channel while the policy is in place. This is why the archive file-naming pattern remains unobserved, and why no automatic archive purge is implemented.

facts.source: Select-String across C:\Windows\PolicyDefinitions\*.admx on the lab
facts.notes: EnablePrefetcher is NOT a Group Policy setting - no ADMX on the target OS declares it. Unlike every other registry value in this toolkit its location cannot be cited to a policy definition, so it is cited to Microsoft documentation and its EFFECT was measured instead. Key: HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management\PrefetchParameters, value EnablePrefetcher, REG_DWORD, 0 disabled / 1 application launch / 2 boot / 3 both.

facts.source: measured repeatedly on the lab (Server 2019, NVMe SSD)
facts.notes: IMPORTANT LIMIT on what Enable-ServerPrefetch can deliver. On a host whose system volume reports MediaType SSD / BusType NVMe / SpindleSpeed 0: EnablePrefetcher=3 was written and read back, SURVIVED the reboot itself, and was then REMOVED again a few minutes into normal operation - observed twice - with NO Group Policy applied (gpresult reported 'N/A') and no AWS agent config referencing prefetch. No .pf file was ever produced, and SysMain was Running and Automatic throughout, so a stopped service was NOT the cause. Windows is understood to disable prefetching on fast media; that is CONSISTENT with what was measured but NOT proven here, because proving it needs a host with rotational media and none was available. Practical consequence: on modern SSD-backed servers, do not promise an MSP that Prefetch will record execution history. Absence of .pf is itself the DFIR-relevant finding.

facts.source: measured on the lab
facts.notes: TRAP for any script built on docs/SCRIPT-TEMPLATE.ps1. PowerShell variable names are case-insensitive and its scoping is dynamic, so the shared Invoke-Main's local '$mode' (holding Audit/Apply/Rollback) MASKS a script PARAMETER named $Mode inside every function Invoke-Main calls. A -Mode parameter silently received the string 'Audit' instead of its own value, and a hashtable lookup on it returned null. '$mode' is effectively reserved: name script parameters something else.

facts.source: observed on the lab while trying to archive the toolkit root
facts.notes: Side effect of our own hardening, worth knowing before an MSP hits it. Once Enable-IRVisibility points PowerShell transcription at <ToolkitRoot>\Transcripts, every live PowerShell session holds a transcript file open in there - so the toolkit root cannot be moved or deleted while any session is running, even by an Administrator: Move-Item fails with 'Access to the path is denied'. Practical consequences: (1) an operator wanting to relocate or clean the toolkit root must roll back transcription first, or do it from a non-PowerShell context; (2) it incidentally makes the evidence directory harder to remove, which is not an accident worth relying on but is a mild bonus; (3) any future script that tries to tidy the toolkit root must expect this and report it rather than assuming a delete succeeded.

facts.notes: Settles a contradiction between Microsoft's documentation and the host. The WEF walkthrough names the forwarder's channel 'Microsoft-Windows-Eventlog-ForwardingPlugin/Operational'. facts.source: Measured 2026-08-25 on the lab.example lab: DC LAB-DC (<lab DC>) and member LAB-MEMBER (<lab member>), both Server 2019 17763.
facts.notes: [adsisearcher] succeeds or fails purely on the CALLER's security context, and the failure text is 'The specified domain either does not exist or could not be contacted' - which reads like a DNS or connectivity fault and is not one. Measured three ways: (1) on the DC, SSH as Administrator resolves to LAB\Administrator, a DOMAIN account (RID 500) - adsisearcher works, RootDSE resolves. (2) on the MEMBER, SSH as Administrator resolves to the LOCAL LAB-MEMBER\Administrator - adsisearcher FAILS and \\domain\SYSVOL gives Access is denied. facts.source: Measured 2026-08-25 on LAB-DC after Install-ADDSForest on Server 2019 17763.
facts.notes: After promotion the DNS server's forwarder list was 'fec0:0:0:ffff::1, fec0:0:0:ffff::2, fec0:0:0:ffff::3, <lab resolver>' - Windows' IPv6 site-local defaults IN FRONT of the working resolver. Nothing answers them, each costs the 3s forwarder timeout, and the DC returned 'DNS server failure' for learn.microsoft.com despite already having a valid forwarder configured. Replacing the list with the single working address fixed it immediately. So a forwarder being PRESENT is not a forwarder being USED: verify by resolving something.

facts.source: Measured 2026-08-25 on LAB-DC, Server 2019 17763, with a Tailscale TUN adapter holding 169.254.83.107.
facts.notes: A second interface with an APIPA address made the DNS server log events 408 and 404 on every start - 'could not open socket for address 169.254.83.107' - because it binds to all interfaces. It had NOT registered that address in the domain zone (RegisterThisConnectionsAddress was already False), which is the failure that would actually break member lookups. Stopping the Tailscale service REMOVED the adapter entirely rather than merely disabling it, and after a DNS service restart the 408/404 errors stopped completely while the domain and external resolution both kept working.

facts.source: Measured 2026-08-25 on lab.example: ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota = 10 on a default Server 2019 forest. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/manage/component-updates/ms-ds-machineaccountquota

facts.source: Measured 2026-08-25 on LAB-MEMBER, Server 2019 17763, 80 GB volume with 54 GB free, journal at 4 GiB.
facts.notes: fsutil usn createjournal EXITS 0 AND DOES NOTHING for any size it will not apply. Requesting 5 GiB, 6 GiB and 8 GiB each exited 0 and left Maximum Size, Allocation Delta and First Usn untouched; requesting 32 MiB and 64 MiB (smaller) did the same. So its exit code is not a statement about whether the size changed - only a read-back is. Consequence: growing a journal past whatever the host will grant is impossible AND unreportable from the exit code, and shrinking one is impossible at all, which makes an enlargement irreversible.

facts.source: Measured 2026-08-25 on the lab.example DC, Server 2019 17763, PS 5.1.
facts.notes: DirectoryEntry.Options (a DirectoryEntryConfiguration) has NO SecurityMasks property - setting it throws "The property 'SecurityMasks' cannot be found on this object", before AND after forcing a bind via NativeObject. SecurityMasks exists on DirectorySearcher only. And DirectoryEntry.ObjectSecurity is not a workaround: it reported ZERO audit rules on an object carrying two, and AddAuditRule on it threw "The system acl cannot be modified as it was not retrieved from the backend store." The working path is DirectorySearcher with SecurityMasks including Sacl, reading ntSecurityDescriptor, then ActiveDirectorySecurity.SetSecurityDescriptorBinaryForm - proven against AdminSDHolder, a 1,356-byte descriptor carrying the 3 audit rules AD ships. Writing back means setting ntSecurityDescriptor to GetSecurityDescriptorBinaryForm() and CommitChanges; proven to add one audit rule with the DACL byte-identical afterwards.

facts.source: Measured 2026-08-25 on CN=AdminSDHolder,CN=System in the lab.example domain.
facts.notes: ActiveDirectorySecurity.AddAuditRule MERGES a new rule into an existing ACE for the same SID, audit flags and inheritance scope, ORing the rights masks - it does not add a second ACE. AdminSDHolder shipped an explicit 0xC0020 Success/None audit ACE; adding 0xD016B Success/None produced ONE ACE at 0xD016B, because 0xC0020 -bor 0xD016B = 0xD016B. That also makes it idempotent - adding the same rule twice left the count unchanged. THE DANGEROUS CONSEQUENCE: a rollback that removes 'the rule we added' removes the pre-existing ACE with it, because they are now the same ACE. On AdminSDHolder that is the loss of a pre-existing audit setting on the object that controls the ACLs of every protected group in the domain, and it had to be restored by hand.

facts.source: Measured 2026-08-25 between LAB-MEMBER (source) and LAB-DC (collector), both Server 2019 17763, same subnet, lab.example.
facts.notes: Collector side verified good: Wecsvc Running/Automatic, ForwardedEvents enabled at 2 GiB, subscription IronBlackBox-Baseline SourceInitiated/Enabled with RunTimeStatus Active and LastError 0, Event Forwarding Plugin registered and Enabled with ResourceUri http://schemas.microsoft.com/wbem/wsman/1/windows/EventLog, AllowedSourceDomainComputers granting Domain Computers and Network Service. Source side verified good: subscription manager policy value registered, NETWORK SERVICE granted read on Security, TCP 5985 to the collector reachable and resolving to the right host. Forwarding still does NOT establish: the source logs Microsoft-Windows-Forwarding/Operational event 105 with error 2150859027, 'The WinRM client sent a request to an HTTP server and got a response saying the requested HTTP URL was not available.' Both hosts have WinRM AllowUnencrypted=false with Kerberos and Negotiate enabled. Not yet diagnosed. Note that a raw unauthenticated POST to /wsman/SubscriptionManager/WEC returns HTTP 404 while /wsman returns 401, and that is NOT evidence of a broken endpoint - WinRM routes authenticated WS-Man envelopes, so the raw probe proves nothing.

facts.source: Measured 2026-08-25 on LAB-DC, the lab.example DC, Server 2019 17763.

facts.source: Measured 2026-08-26 on LAB-MEMBER (member) and LAB-DC (DC), Server 2019 17763.9121, via 'auditpol /backup'.
facts.notes: Windows Server 2019 enables 17 audit subcategories out of the box: Account Lockout 1, Audit Policy Change 1, Authentication Policy Change 1, Computer Account Management 1, Credential Validation 1, Directory Service Access 1, Kerberos Authentication Service 1, Kerberos Service Ticket Operations 1, Logoff 1, Logon 3, Network Policy Server 3, Other System Events 3, Security Group Management 1, Security State Change 1, Special Logon 1, System Integrity 3, User Account Management 1. facts.source: A/B measured 2026-08-25 on LAB-MEMBER, each subcategory enabled alone under identical WMI/vssadmin/tasklist load for ~30s.
facts.notes: Token Right Adjusted {0CCE924A} alone produced 104 x 4703. Authorization Policy Change {0CCE9231} alone produced 0 x 4703. Both off produced 0. The learn.microsoft.com page for Audit Authorization Policy Change lists 4703 in its event list; on Server 2019 that is wrong. This is why Token Right Adjusted is excluded (volume) and Authorization Policy Change is enabled (it is low-volume without 4703).

facts.source: A/B measured 2026-08-25 on LAB-MEMBER against a single 'gpupdate /force'; host carried 484 WFP filters.
facts.notes: Other Policy Change Events {0CCE9234} at Success produced 630 x 5447 per gpupdate. Filtering Platform Policy Change {0CCE9233} at Success produced 0 x 5447. facts.source: Measured 2026-08-26 on LAB-MEMBER with Authorization Policy Change and Authentication Policy Change both enabled; rights granted via secedit.
facts.notes: Granting SeDebugPrivilege (a privilege) produced 4704 'a user right was assigned' plus 4717/4718. So 4704/4705 come from Authorization Policy Change and cover privileges, while logon-right grants surface as 4717/4718 under Authentication Policy Change. A test that grants a logon right and expects 4704 will wrongly conclude the subcategory is dead.

facts.source: Measured 2026-08-26 on LAB-MEMBER.

facts.source: Measured 2026-08-26 on LAB-MEMBER with a distinctive value (1572864 KB) nothing else uses. SUPERSEDES the 2026-08-23 note in docs/VALIDATION.md that said a reboot was required.
facts.notes: Writing MaxSize to the Security policy key left the channel unchanged, and unchanged after a 3s wait. facts.source: Measured 2026-08-26 on LAB-MEMBER.

facts.source: Measured 2026-08-26 on LAB-MEMBER, Server 2019 17763.9121.
facts.notes: 'wevtutil gl <channel>' emits, indented under a 'logging:' heading, 'logFileName: %SystemRoot%\\System32\\Winevt\\Logs\\Security.evtx' and 'maxSize: 1073741824'. The path keeps its environment variable UNEXPANDED, so a caller must run it through ExpandEnvironmentVariables before touching the filesystem. This is how Enable-IRVisibility finds the volume a channel actually lands on instead of assuming C: - a channel can be relocated to another disk, and sizing it then authorises growth on a volume that was never measured. UNVERIFIED: whether the 'logFileName' key name is localised on a non-English host; the code fails closed if the key is not found.

facts.source: Measured 2026-08-27 on LAB-MEMBER against Set-TimelineIntegrity, Enable-Sysmon and Protect-ForensicArtifacts.
facts.notes: lab/Invoke-LabCycle.sh judged the rollback step by grepping stdout for the literal 'Rollback complete'. facts.source: Measured 2026-08-27 in BOTH directions on LAB-DC (collector, 7.9 GB RAM) with LAB-MEMBER as the source.
facts.notes: Above roughly 3.5 GB of RAM Windows hosts each service in its own svchost process. WinRM then owns the single URL reservation 'HTTP://+:5985/WSMAN/' and Wecsvc, in a different process, CANNOT register 'HTTP://+:5985/WSMAN/SUBSCRIPTIONMANAGER/WEC/'. A source enumerating resourceUri http://schemas.microsoft.com/wbem/wsman/1/SubscriptionManager/Subscription is answered by WinRM, which has no handler for that sub-path, and gets WS-Man 2150859027 'the requested HTTP URL was not available' - surfaced as event 105 in Microsoft-Windows-Forwarding/Operational. SPLIT: Wecsvc PID 3200, WinRM PID 3088, one reservation. MERGED (SvcHostSplitDisable=1 under BOTH Services\\Wecsvc AND Services\\WinRM, then a REBOOT): both PID 776, three reservations including SUBSCRIPTIONMANAGER/WEC. Setting it on Wecsvc alone is NOT enough - measured, a service restart is not enough either, svchost grouping is decided at boot. After merging: WinRM event 142 'Enumeration failed 2150859027' became 132 'Enumeration completed successfully', wecutil gr gained an EventSources section with heartbeats, and 145 events forwarded end to end.

facts.source: Measured 2026-08-27 on LAB-DC, before and after the W-1 fix.

Documented ceiling cited from https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/wes/consuming-events
facts.notes: Microsoft documents the limit verbatim: 'If the XPath expression is a compound expression that contains more than 20 expressions or you are querying for events from multiple sources, then you must use a structured XML query.' Using a structured XML query (QueryList/Query/Select) does NOT lift the limit - it is how you stay under it, by spreading terms across several Select elements, as the sample on that page shows. Measured tolerance on this build: 23 EventID terms in one <Select> is accepted, 24 is refused. Isolated three ways: (1) it is the TERM COUNT, not the string length - a 22-term query padded to a 529-character XPath, longer than the 24-term query's 393, was accepted; (2) it is not a toxic event ID - the first 13 and the last 13 of the list each worked alone; (3) it is PER-SELECTOR, not per-subscription - all 26 IDs across two Select elements worked, as did three Selects and two Query elements on the same channel, and the subscription carries 36 terms across three channels.

When the overlong channel is the only one, the subscription fails outright with event 102, error code 5004. Throughout the 101 state the collector reports RunTimeStatus Active, LastError 0 and a fresh heartbeat, and 'wecutil gr' shows the source under EventSources - so no collector-side indicator reveals the missing channel. The 101's Status field is a <t:QueryStatus> document with one <t:Channel Name=... ErrorCode=.../> per channel in the query - the unreadable channel carries a non-zero code (Security ErrorCode=15001 for the W-2 case) while the others are 0. facts.source: Measured 2026-08-27 on LAB-MEMBER (Server 2019 build 17763.9121) against live 100/101/102 subscriptions. Evidence: the review log kept in the development repository 'W-2'.
facts.notes: On every policy refresh the forwarder emits event 103 (unsubscribed) for each subscription it currently holds, then a fresh 100/101/102 for each subscription the collector still offers. Two consequences for reading this channel: (1) a subscription whose NEWEST event is 103 is one the host no longer carries; (2) a 102 never receives a 103 - you cannot unsubscribe what was never subscribed - so a failed subscription the collector has since removed would be reported forever unless verdicts older than the channel's newest 103 are discarded. A time window is NOT a usable substitute: the SubscriptionManager value carries Refresh=60, so rounds are a minute apart, and a 120-second window was measured leaking a deleted subscription back as a finding 46 seconds later. Correlation ActivityID does not group a round either - it tracks the WinRM process instance and spans several rounds.

facts.source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/operating-system-security/device-management/use-windows-event-forwarding-to-assist-in-intrusion-detection
facts.notes: Microsoft's published WEF baseline is structured as 43 separate <Query> elements, each with a short <Select> - independent confirmation of the W-2 fix, since it never puts many IDs in one selector. It also uses <Suppress> and per-field predicates for noise that IronBlackBox forwards unfiltered: 5140 only when ShareName is neither \\*\IPC$ nor \\*\NetLogon; 4672 suppressed where the subject SID is S-1-5-18; 4624 split by LogonType, with network logons (type 3) moved out of the baseline into a separate 'Suspect' subscription. Stated WEC ceiling: '3,000 events per second on average for all configured subscriptions'. On ContentFormat: RenderedText means 'the event size is effectively doubled or tripled', and the Events (binary) format 'can more than double the event volume a single WEC server can accommodate'. facts.source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/operating-system-security/device-management/use-windows-event-forwarding-to-assist-in-intrusion-detection , and measured 2026-08-28 on the lab.
facts.notes: Microsoft: 'suppress statements that filter out specific events, only apply within that query statement'. A <Suppress> therefore applies to EVERY <Select> in its <Query>, not just one. Consequence for a multi-ID Security query: a <Suppress> for SubjectUserSid=S-1-5-18 intended to drop SYSTEM's 4672 would also delete every 4688 (process create) whose subject is SYSTEM - measured 1227 of 3032 on the member (40%) and 565 of 1124 on the DC (50%), i.e. services and SYSTEM-run tasks. The safe pattern is an INLINE predicate appended to a single <Select> for a single event id (e.g. '*[System[(EventID=4672)]] and *[EventData[Data[@Name="SubjectUserSid"] != "S-1-5-18"]]'), which can only ever affect that one id. Verified with Get-WinEvent -FilterXPath using the subscription's own predicate string: it selects exactly the intended side (0 SYSTEM survive the 4672 keep-filter; 0 IPC$/NetLogon survive the 5140 keep-filter) and forwarding of SYSTEM-spawned 4688 was unaffected.

facts.source: Measured 2026-08-28 on LAB-MEMBER.
facts.notes: Get-WinEvent -FilterXPath pages by RecordId with '*[System[(EventID=N) and EventRecordID > K]]' using the RAW '>' operator. The XML-escaped form '>' THROWS 'The specified query is invalid'. This is the opposite of a structured XML <QueryList> query, where '>' must be escaped. RecordId is monotonic and unique per channel, so this is the correct way to read a channel incrementally without loss: a timestamp bookmark cannot advance through events that share a second (measured: a 5-event cap over a same-second burst re-read the same five forever), whereas EventRecordID > lastMax always advances. Scan -Oldest so the cap keeps the oldest and the last element carries the highest RecordId processed.

facts.source: Measured 2026-08-28 on LAB-MEMBER.

'InvalidNamespace' (HRESULT 0x8004100E) means the namespace does not exist - benign, e.g. querying root\thisdoesnotexist, or root\default absent on some hosts. 'InvalidClass' means the class is not registered in that namespace - benign, e.g. ActiveScriptEventConsumer does not exist in root\cimv2. Any OTHER failure (access denied, provider fault) means the namespace/class is present but could not be READ, which a collector must not treat as 'absent'. facts.source: Measured 2026-09-02 on Server 2019 Datacenter 17763 via 'Get-WinEvent -ListLog <channel>' and cross-checked against 'wevtutil gl' type.
facts.notes: Get-WinEvent -ListLog exposes IsClassicLog, which separates the logs the EventLog policy governs from the ones it does not, as a property of the channel rather than a guess from its name. True: Security, Application, System, and 'Windows PowerShell'. False: Microsoft-Windows-SmbClient/Security, Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational. facts.source: Measured 2026-09-02 on Server 2019 Datacenter 17763: Protect-EventLogs -Apply -Channels 'Microsoft-Windows-SmbClient/Security', with 'wevtutil gl' read before and after.
facts.notes: Retention and AutoBackupLogFiles under HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\EventLog\<channel> govern CLASSIC logs only. Pointed at a modern channel the write SUCCEEDS and has no effect: the policy key was created with AutoBackupLogFiles=1 and Retention=1, the registry read them back, the script reported '2 change(s) applied' and exited 0, and 'wevtutil gl' reported retention:false both before and after. Same family as the AT-13 lesson that the policy MaxSize value cannot size a modern channel - and the same trap in the other direction: there it did nothing visible, here it reported success. Consequence: a script that writes this policy must test IsClassicLog first, and a modern channel gets capacity through 'wevtutil sl /ms:' with no archive-on-full equivalent that this project has found.

facts.source: Measured 2026-09-02 on Server 2019 Datacenter 17763: 'wevtutil sl Microsoft-Windows-SmbClient/Security /ms:9000000' then 'wevtutil gl' on the same channel.
facts.notes: This repository asserts in the review log kept in the development repository and in Enable-IRVisibility's channel-sizing comment that wevtutil rounds /ms: up to a 64 KB multiple, and NO facts.json row backed that. Measured: a request for 9000000 bytes - not a multiple of 65536 - produced a channel reporting maxSize 9000000 exactly. So no rounding occurred on that channel at that value.\n\nDELIBERATELY MARKED PARTIAL. One value on one modern channel does not refute the general claim: rounding may apply to classic logs, to other value ranges, or to the EventLog policy path rather than to 'sl /ms:'. What this row establishes is only that the claim is NOT universally true and was never grounded. Consequence for code: a read-back that compares exactly is wrong wherever rounding does occur, and a read-back that only tests '>=' the requested size passes a channel that never changed - so the comparison has to be one-sided with a small tolerance, which is what Restore-EventChannelChange now does.

facts.source: Measured 2026-09-02 on Server 2019 Datacenter 17763, single 80 GB MBR disk: first with a 12 GB VHD attached as D:, then with a real 15 GB partition created as D: after shrinking C: online.
facts.notes: 'vssadmin add shadowstorage /for=C: /on=D:' is REFUSED with "The specified volume is nested too deeply to participate in the VSS operation" when D: is a VHD whose backing file lives on C:. The same command is ACCEPTED when D: is a real partition, even on the same physical disk. So the error is about a backing file on the protected volume, not about sharing a spindle.\n\nConsequence for this project: a relocated shadow storage area can be exercised on a one-disk lab without attaching a second EBS volume. Shrink C: with Resize-Partition, New-Partition, Format-Volume, then add the association. That is how the second half of V-1 was finally proven - event 4688 captured 'vssadmin.exe resize shadowstorage /for=C: /on=D: /maxsize=4187467038', which is the operating system's own record of the argument construction rather than a reading of the code.

facts.source: measured on Windows 11 Pro build 26200 and Windows Server 2019 build 17763, 2026-09-09
facts.notes: TRAP, and it produced a false positive on every Windows 11 endpoint. 'powershell.exe -Version 2' does NOT reliably fail when the v2 engine is absent. On Windows 11 build 26200 it prints 'PowerShell 2.0 has been deprecated. Using default PowerShell instead.', RUNS THE COMMAND UNDER 5.1, and EXITS 0. Remove-PowerShellV2 read that 0 as proof the engine ran and raised 'PowerShell 2.0 CAN RUN on this host - ScriptBlock logging can be bypassed' - an exposure that does not exist, as a finding no -Apply could clear, on a whole fleet of workstations. On Server 2019 the same switch exits non-zero (-65536 with .NET 3.5 missing, -327680 with the engine registry key missing), which is why the exit code looked sufficient. THE FIX: ask the child what version it is and read the answer - major 2 means a v2 engine really ran, major 5 means the switch fell back. Pass the probe with -EncodedCommand, not -Command: inner double quotes are stripped during argument handling, the child gets a syntax error and exits 1, and the probe then reports 'engine unavailable' for a malformed command - which on a host where v2 DOES run would be a false ALL-CLEAR. Do not match a bare digit either: the deprecation notice contains the digit 2.

facts.source: vssadmin verb lists compared side by side, 2026-09-09: Windows 11 Pro build 26200 against Windows Server 2019 build 17763
facts.notes: A CLIENT SKU CANNOT CREATE A SHADOW STORAGE ASSOCIATION. Measured: 'vssadmin' on Windows 11 offers Delete Shadows, List Providers, List Shadows, List ShadowStorage, List Volumes, List Writers and Resize ShadowStorage. Server 2019 offers all of those PLUS Add ShadowStorage, Delete ShadowStorage and Query Reverts. Win32_ShadowStorage IS present on the client with a Create method, and Create answers RETURN CODE 10 - a value absent from Microsoft's documented set (1 access denied, 2 invalid argument, 3 volume not found, 4 volume not supported, 11 insufficient storage). Enable-VssPreservation threw on that unmapped code and the run exited 2, which docs/DEPLOYMENT.md section 2 tells an MSP to alert as a BROKEN DEPLOYMENT - on every workstation in a fleet, for a capability Windows never offered and no -Apply can supply. It is now reported as a host limit, out of the exit code. WHAT STILL WORKS ON A CLIENT: resizing an association Windows or System Restore already made, and Enable-VssSnapshotSchedule's snapshot task, which passed its full cycle on the same host. The detection is by ProductType and not by parsing the vssadmin verb list, because that list is localised and this project does not read localised prose to decide what a script may do.
